guarantees.claim: unused_cfg_shadowed_qe is the XOR reduction of all QE bits from the shadowed configuration registers (kmac_en, kstrength, mode, msg_endianness, state_endianness, sideload, entropy_mode, entropy_fast_process, msg_mask, en_unsupported_modestrength).
alert_test[1] is the logical AND of reg2hw.alert_test.fatal_fault_err.q and .qe; alert_test[0] is the logical AND of reg2hw.alert_test.recov_operation_err.q and .qe.
alerts[1] is driven by alert_fatal; alerts[0] is driven by alert_recov_operation.
alert_recov_operation is directly driven by shadowed_update_err.

assumptions.claim: The signals shadowed_update_err and alert_fatal are correctly generated by external logic to indicate a shadow register update error and a fatal fault, respectively.
assumptions.risk: If these signals are incorrect or stuck, the alert outputs will not reflect true error conditions, possibly hiding security‑critical faults.

uncertain_points.claim: unused_cfg_shadowed_qe computes XOR of all shadowed register QE bits. A reliable integrity check for shadowed registers requires all QE bits to be 1 (AND); XOR is parity and can miss double‑bit errors or partial writes. It is unclear whether this signal is used downstream for error detection or is intentionally dead logic.
uncertain_points.cond: If unused_cfg_shadowed_qe is connected to any error logic.
uncertain_points.risk: A false sense of shadowed‑register integrity may be induced, allowing undetected configuration corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: Signal unused_cfg_shadowed_qe is computed but its name suggests it may be deliberately unconnected. If it is unused, it represents dead logic with no functional impact.
uncertain_points.cond: If the signal is not used elsewhere in the module.
uncertain_points.risk: Dead code can confuse verification and maintenance, but poses no direct security risk if truly unused.

uncertain_points.claim: The recoverable alert alert_recov_operation is directly driven by shadowed_update_err. The comment on line 1431-1432 states the alert is observable until the KMAC operation is restarted, implying shadowed_update_err must remain asserted (sticky) until that restart. The actual sticky behavior is not defined in this chunk and must be confirmed in the logic that generates shadowed_update_err.
uncertain_points.cond: When a shadowed update error occurs.
uncertain_points.risk: If shadowed_update_err is not sticky, the alert may be deasserted before software can observe the error, violating the documented observability requirement.
